defects: Environment is underexposed and murky: the brick walls, road and building masses crush to near-black with little falloff detail, so the street reads as a dark game-engine blockout rather than a lit set
The dark sky and wall gradients risk banding and macroblocking; the shadows look muddy, not graded
Whip transitions use one heavy directional smear (pairs row 1) that wipes out the sign typography for several frames, which reads as a stock blur rather than shaped camera motion
Chromatic-aberration and RGB-split fringes on the title letters (the T, N and S edges) are applied evenly as a filter instead of being motivated per material
The 'WRITTEN & DIRECTED BY' sign goes soft and scanline-ghosted mid-move, so the credit is unreadable for part of its screen time
Credit signs look flat-lit, with no light spill from the bright sign faces onto the wet ground or the walls, so the emitters don't sit in the scene
The final frames lose letters ('NIGHT HO S'); the flicker-out reads as missing glyphs rather than a designed resolve
Repeated camera grammar: nearly every credit is the same dolly-past-a-sign-on-the-left move at the same speed
gaps: Motion: the credits repeat one move, a forward street dolly plus whip to the next sign, roughly every 0.9 s. Top work would vary the camera (crane, lateral track, rack focus, reflections in puddles) and give the signs their own behaviour (ignition, buzz, failing tubes) so each credit has its own beat. The 4.2 s title hold needs in-shot life, not just a static flicker

Finish: the lighting and world-building don't match the type design. The halftone, LED, neon and stripe letter materials at 100% are good, but the street around them is underlit and has no volumetrics, wet-surface reflections, emitter bounce or atmospheric haze, so the 'night' is just darkness. Grade the blacks, add light falloff from every sign, and remove the generic chromatic-aberration overlay

Sound and ending: the score is a regular grid of transients with a filtered drop at about 7.6–8.4 s and a broadband slam at the title. It is effective but formulaic: there is little sign-specific sound design (neon hum, relay clicks, rain, traffic) tied to the individual credits, and the tail fades thinly. The end doesn't settle or rhyme with the opening street shot, and it closes on a glitch rather than a composed final lockup
